newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's December diesel likely to be small - traders.
newsitem.headline: India's December diesel likely to be small - traders.

text.p: India, one of the region's largest diesel consumer, is not likely to purchase large volumes of diesel for delivery in December, industry sources said on Monday.
"At the moment the evidence does not show that they would buy a lot in December. There are four to five ships waiting to discharge in each port," one trader said.
Trading sources said India had not cleared the backlog of tankers waiting to discharge at the key ports of Goa, Kandla and Madras.
According to their estimates, there are about one million tonnes of diesel waiting to discharge at these ports.
India had reduced its diesel purchases sharply over the past few months and had cancelled a tender to import cargoes for November delivery.
For the first six months of the year, state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC), the country's sole diesel importer, bought a total of about six million tonnes.
But between July and October it bought a mere 1.76 million tonnes.
Trading sources said the lower imports were partly due to increase in term imports by IOC.

IOC had increased or maintained its term imports with Middle East producers such as Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC), Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) and Bahrain National Oil Co (BANOCO) for a total of about 3.53 million tonnes.
It is for first time trying to secure up to one million tonnes of diesel from Saudi Aramco on a term basis for 1997, but no news has been known so far on whether or not a deal has been struck.

IOC had also awarded an additional term contract to traders this year compared to 1995. For the year beginning July 1996 to June 1997 IOC awarded three contracts through tenders for the purchase of a 45,000-tonne cargo each month.
"It appears as if IOC has asked its term suppliers to increase the quantity supplied. If you look at the number of ships in queue, it's not going down," one trader said.

As a result, traders told Reuters that there is a possibility IOC might even not issue a diesel import tender for December. Others said that if they do decide to issue one, the tender will be floated this week.
Most are of the opinion that IOC is likely to take two or three cargoes in December, but this could change if the demurrage problem clears up in a month's time.
